correctness.rationale: The pinned 24-edge four-regular Chvatal graph and 0->1 only upon excited-neighbor, 1->2->3->0 rule were reconstructed directly from the package and its two independent C++ implementations. Independent C++ functional-graph enumeration built every successor over all 4^12=16,777,216 labelled states (no sampling), removed zero-indegree vertices, traversed every residual cycle and back-propagated depths. It obtained one fixed state, 29,602 primitive four-cycles (118,408 rotating states), period-1 basin 3,791,756, exactly 21 joint depth/period cells, maximum first entry 12 and 48 maximizers; hence F^16=F^12. Independently evaluating the local successor-supported four-color predicate gives 118,408. Full NetworkX graph automorphism enumeration found eight automorphisms, six orbits of eight extremal states with exactly the six stated representatives. This proves a finite fixed-graph census, not arbitrary graphs; only period-dividing-four recurrence is characterized structurally, while the exhaustive functional graph excludes other periods.
residual_risks: Exact statement confined to labelled 12-vertex Chvatal graph and q=4 threshold one; no unbounded family classification.

value.rationale: The Chvatal graph is the canonical smallest 4-regular triangle-free 4-chromatic graph, making its finite deterministic four-state excitation dynamics a motivated exact model rather than an arbitrary small sample. The complete 16.8-million-state classification, 12-step sharp cutoff and six extremal automorphism orbits identify meaningful dynamics and symmetry that qualitative graph theory does not predict. It is a finite exact invariant of a natural graph, not an asserted universal graph theorem.
